props.name: series
props.description: Series drawn as dots unless they set a `type`

props.name: height
props.description: Height of the chart (the legend included); numbers are pixels

props.name: width
props.description: Width of the chart; numbers are pixels

props.name: renderer
props.description: Backend of the data layer: `auto` tries WebGPU, then WebGL2, then WebGL, then Canvas2D

props.name: legend
props.description: Legend; shown by default when several series have a name

props.name: crosshair
props.description: Vertical guide line following the pointer

props.name: interaction
props.description: Zoom (Ctrl / ⌘ + wheel, pinch), pan (drag), double-click reset and keyboard navigation; `false` makes the chart static

props.name: padding
props.description: Space around the plot area, in pixels

props.name: palette
props.description: Series colors (defaults to the `--chart-series-1..8` CSS variables, then the theme colors)

props.name: locale
props.description: Locale of the texts and numbers the chart writes (tooltip rows, compact units `k` / `万`, separators, month and weekday names of time axes)

props.name: labels
props.description: Overrides of the built-in texts of the `locale`

props.name: renderTooltip
props.description: React content of the tooltip (replaces the default content)

events.name: onHover
events.description: Called when the hovered (or keyboard-focused) points change

events.name: onPointClick
events.description: Called when a point (or bar) is clicked

events.name: onPlotClick
events.description: Called when the plot area is clicked where there is no point

events.name: onZoom
events.description: Called when the user zooms or pans

events.name: onRendererChange
events.description: Called with the backend once it is ready (and when it falls back after a GPU loss)

props.name: series
props.description: Series drawn as dots unless they set a `type`

examples.title: Basic
examples.description: Two series of [x, y] tuples with axis titles; the tooltip shows the nearest dot.

examples.title: Categories
examples.description: One series per category gives each group its own color and a legend entry that toggles it; here three penguin species by flipper length and body mass.

examples.title: Labels and sizes
examples.description: Point objects carry a label and a size; showLabels draws the labels, skipping overlaps.

examples.title: 200,000 points
examples.description: Two Gaussian clusters as typed-array columns; hit testing uses a spatial index.

examples.title: Live sensor stream
examples.description: A new vibration sample every 400 ms (a setInterval cleared on pause and on unmount), split into a normal and an alarm series around a reference line; fixed min and max keep the axes still while the data streams in.

examples.title: Log-log axes
examples.description: xAxis and yAxis with type: "log" turn the power law of the metabolic rates (Kleiber's law) into a straight line across six orders of magnitude; the fit is a two-point line series with tooltip: false.

examples.title: Outliers
examples.description: Per-point color, size and label flag the requests much slower than expected for their payload; the expected time is a line series.

examples.title: Custom tooltip and regions
examples.description: renderTooltip replaces the tooltip with React content built from the demo data. The league averages are dashed reference lines, and rect annotations with open bounds shade two corners up to the edges of the plot.

examples.title: Click to select
examples.description: onPointClick gives the series and the index of the clicked dot: the selected employee gets a bigger dot and a label, and their details appear below. onPlotClick, called on the empty plot, clears the selection.

examples.title: Correlation and trend
examples.description: A least-squares trend line (a line series computed in the demo) over the campaigns, with a text annotation giving R² and the slope.

examples.title: Zoom controls
examples.description: Buttons zoom to regions through the ref: setView sets the visible range (it does not call onZoom, so the demo reads the view back with getView) and resetZoom shows everything again. onZoom reports the wheel and drag zooms; a rect annotation shades the growing range.

ScatterChartProps.series: Series drawn as dots unless they set a type

basic.title: Basic
basic.description: Two clusters of dots with axis titles; tap a dot to read its series and values.

clusters.title: Two clusters
clusters.description: [x, y] pairs of two series with axis titles; zoom on both axes with Ctrl / ⌘ + wheel.

point-click.title: Clicked point
point-click.description: Labelled points; clicking one shows its label and values (point click event).

props.height: Height of the chart, the legend included: pixels or any CSS length
props.options: Other engine options (axes, legend, tooltip, palette, format…) merged with the element's own properties; property only
props.instance: The engine instance (minerva-design/charts/core), null until the element is rendered and connected

events.minerva-hover: The hovered (or keyboard-focused) points changed; detail: { x, xLabel, items }, null when nothing is hovered
events.minerva-point-click: A point or a bar was clicked; detail: { x, xLabel, items }
events.minerva-plot-click: The plot area was clicked where there is no point; detail: { x, y } in data coordinates
events.minerva-zoom: The user zoomed or panned; detail: { x, y } (the visible ranges)
events.minerva-renderer-change: The backend is ready, or fell back after a GPU loss; detail: { renderer }

methods.getView: Visible range, null before the engine is created
methods.getRenderer: Backend in use (webgpu, webgl2, webgl, canvas2d), null until ready
